title.narrative: National Democratic Institute Burkina Faso: Paving the way to democratic success
National Democratic Institute Burkina Faso: Paving the way to democratic success

description.narrative:
Programme goal: Building democratic resilience during and beyond the transition in Burkina Faso.
Objective 1: Burkinabe civil society promotes democratic processes and accountability.
Objective 2: Informed and organized citizens participate in political and democratic processes.
Objective 3: Political parties adopt reforms for better inclusivity and responsiveness to citizens priorities.

National Democratic Institute (NDI) föreslår ett program med det övergripande målet att hållbart stärka den demokratiska motståndskraften under och efter övergångsperioden. Programmet kommer att stödja det burkinska civilsamhället i att aktivt delta i demokratiska processer, att främja ansvarsskyldighet, att informera medborgarna om politiska och demokratiska processer för att främja deras engagemang och deltagande. Programmet kommer vidare att ge tekniskt stöd till politiska partier för att anta reformer i syfte att bli mer inkluderande och lyhörda inför medborgarnas prioriteringar.

The National Democratic Institute proposes a program with the overarching goal of durably building democratic resilience during and beyond the transition. The program would support Burkinabe civil society in participating actively in democratic processes and promoting accountability, seek to inform citizens about political and democratic processes to foster engagement and participation and provide technical assistance to political parties in adopting reforms to become more inclusive and responsive to citizens’ priorities.

Between November 2022 and December 2024, the National Democratic Institute (NDI) implemented the programme "Paving the way to democratic success" (Democracie Gnie Sera) in Burkina Faso. The final total programme budget was 29 MSEK. The original budget was 35 MSEK, which was decreased in April 2024 due to Sweden's phase out in Burkina Faso.
The overall goal of the programme was building democratic resilience during and beyond the transition in Burkina Faso. Programme main targets were young people and women. The programme was implemented in 12 communes in the country, and covered a range of topics such as civic education, local governance and social cohesion, young people's political engagement, information integrity and reform monitoring.
A diverse array of activities - including educational talks, radio broadcasts, podcasts, conferences, theatrical forums, training sessions, and dialogue sessions with local authorities - engaged at least 283 000 people across the 12 intervention zones. Taking into account social media interactions, the figure is estimated at 350 977 individuals. Through capacity building initiatives and interactive exchanges with local authorities, the programme encouraged participants to take an active interest in and contribute to local governance.
NDI had strategic partnerships through subgrants with six partner civil society organisations (CSOs) working on i) citizen monitoring, ii) effectiveness of anti-corruption policies and support to parliament in human rights based reforms, iii) promoting information integrity, iv) civic education and citizen participation in political transition, v) communication and civic education for citizen participation, and vi) participation of women and young people in democratic governance. NDI also implemented its own activities. Capacity development has been part of the support to the local partners. NDI also collaborated with other CSOs.
In light of Sweden's phase out, Sida's reduced budget to NDI and the changed context, in particular the Burkinabe government's suspension of political parties and authorities' lack of openness to reform, programme modifications were made in April 2024. The programme activity period was shortened with three months (from end date 31 March 2025 to December 2024). Most activities under objective 3 were removed as the programme could no longer work with political parties or provide institutional support to the National Assembly addressing reform change. Instead, the inter-party dialogue committee (CDIP) was supported and training courses for young leaders were carried out. Community days to strengthen social cohesion were expanded. There was also a shift to more activities on information integrity as disinformation became a growing challenge.
During the programme period, risks for partners increased. This had substantial impact on some expected results in comparison to the plan (the original and the updated from April 2024). One example is a civil society partner working with digital awareness-raising on disinformation. The partner planned a digital campaign for large-scale outreach, which had to be cancelled as the information space closed and civil society became more targeted. Instead of the planned reach of over 550 000 persons, the activity was redirected to inperson engagements for safety reasons, and reached over 100 persons. A planned study to assess citizens' perception of governance, reconciliation and social cohesion was cancelled due to risks of political reprisals and potential self-censorship.
Despite the difficult political context, shrinking space, the deterioration of the security situation, Sida's early termination, and the removal of several activities, a large share of the objectives and intermediate results were achieved. NDI's quick adaptation and Sida's flexibility facilitated the adjustments and results achievements.
The final internal evaluation concluded that: "In a challenging socio-security context, the program has played a vital role in fostering unity, social cohesion, and peaceful coexistence. By helping communities overcome socio-cultural, ethnic, and religious divides, it has strengthened the fabric of society and promoted a shared sense of belonging".
Examples of results
Objective 1: Burkinabe civil society promotes democratic processes and accountability
- CSOs launched the National Government Action Monitoring Committee, establishing a permanent platform for CSOs to track government reforms, share updates, and offer recommendations.
- Throughout the programme, one partner surveyed communities across 12 zones to capture citizens perceptions of the transition government's reforms and identify their priorities. The partner monitored all 13 reforms under the second axis of the action plan for stabilisation and development (PASD), and highlighted critical gaps in both the design and rollout of these reforms.
- Partners engaged with transitional authorities, including the transitional legislature, during the ongoing political transition, to advocate for citizen priorities.
- One NDI partner spearheaded stakeholder dialogue sessions and awareness campaigns on anti-corruption, following the transitional authorities' focus on anti-corruption reforms. A national survey on public perceptions on anti-corruption was carried out. The survey results were shared and discussed. Social media campaigns to raise awareness on anti-corruption were carried out.
- NDI in collaboration with international actors organised nine democratic dialogues on information manipulation efforts and democracy. A total of 1800 participants attended the discussions. Subsequent activities led to key recommendations to civil society and international NGOs, such as to continue to advocate for constitutional order, deconstruct false messages and promote rule of law.
Objective 2: Informed and organized citizens participate in political and democratic processes
- NDIs partners conducted civic education campaigns across the five project zones through educational talks, plays and community days, on topics such as citizen engagement, political agency, responsible citizenship, women and youth's rights and citizen monitoring of government action and social cohesion. After the activities, members of the communes were reported adopting more civic-minded and responsible attitudes; expressing that for the first time they felt empowered to approach local authorities directly, voice their concerns, and seek practical solutions; and making personal and collective pledges to continue fostering social cohesion. Some civic initiatives continued.
- Citizens reported back that they participate in political and democratic processes. The baseline was 10,69%, and after year 1 20%. Due to the phase out, the indicator was not followed after that.
- Civic education media campaigns were organised through radio shows and radio spots. One partner hosted radio shows with governance experts who discussed the concepts of local governance and governance in times of transitions and in times of constitutional order. The provincial radio station reaches between 700,000 and one million people. Another partner brodcast 3 radio spots 180 times on the three most listened-to radio stations in the localities, on the role of women and young people in their communities. These messages reached an estimated 56,385 individuals according to listeners statistics.
- Young people received capacity building in how to conduct civic education media campaigns through podcasts: monitoring actions in communities and suggested strategies were identified, and podcasts produced.
Objective 3: Political parties adopt reforms for better inclusivity and responsiveness to citizens priorities.
- In response to a government decree banning formal political party activities, the programme mobilised the committee for interparty dialogue (Comité de Dialogue Interpartis - CDIP), with members from political parties, as a working group to build consensus on needed reforms to become more inclusive of women and youth, maintaining dialogue on transitional reforms, expand existing inter-party dialogue efforts and respond to citizen priorities.
- To prepare political parties for a more inclusive future, NDI provided technical assistance to draft a Code of Conduct promoting citizen-centered political practices. Additionally, CDIP members reviewed and recommended reforms to the legal framework governing political parties.
- Through its Young Leaders Academy, NDI trained 90 young leaders, including political party members, equipping them with practical skills and knowledge to engage effectively in politics once civic space reopens.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
